title: The dream of Blue Texas
gist: Yglesias says Democrat Gina Hinojosa is within striking distance but still behind Greg Abbott in the 2026 Texas governor's race, and betting markets rightly favor Abbott. He frames it as a missed opportunity because she lacks a pre-campaign moderate profile and because Republicans now hold the fundraising edge that Democrats enjoyed in 2018-2020.

insights.claim: Polls show Democrat Gina Hinojosa within striking distance of Texas Governor Greg Abbott but still clearly behind in the 2026 race.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Texas statewide policy (energy, taxes, regulation) likely stays under Republican control.
insights.quote: The polls show her within striking distance but definitely behind.

insights.claim: A Hinojosa win in Texas would require either a meaningful pro-Democratic polling error or a new development that further damages Abbott; Yglesias would not bank on a polling error.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Upset risk in Texas is tail risk, not base case.
insights.quote: For her to win you’d need there to be a meaningful polling error in Democrats’ favor (which is conceptually possible but I wouldn’t bank on it) or for something new to happen in the race that deals a further blow to Abbott.

insights.claim: Betting markets heavily favor Greg Abbott to win re-election as Texas governor, and Yglesias sees no reason to doubt those odds.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Prediction-market pricing aligns with an informed pundit view; little edge in fading it.
insights.quote: The betting odds heavily favor Greg Abbott, and I don’t see any reason to doubt that.

insights.claim: Hinojosa has run a smart moderate-positioned campaign featuring law-enforcement endorsements, a January 6 participant supporting her, and low-tax messaging, despite lacking a pre-campaign moderate reputation.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Democrats in red states are converging on law-and-order and low-tax messaging, signaling a rightward strategic shift.

insights.claim: Yglesias argues the ideal statewide Democratic candidate in Texas would be a Hispanic moderate from South Texas, such as Vicente Gonzalez or former Representative Filemon Vela.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Points to where Democratic competitiveness in Texas could come from in future cycles.
insights.quote: The ideal profile for a statewide Democratic candidate in Texas would be a Hispanic moderate from South Texas.

insights.claim: Democrats had a large financial edge in the early Trump election cycles, but money now favors Republicans in the 2026 cycle.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Funding scarcity constrains Democrats' ability to expand the map, affecting midterm seat outcomes.
insights.quote: The other is just that while Democrats had a big financial edge in the early Trump election cycles, the money now favors Republicans.

insights.claim: In a 2018- or 2020-style fundraising environment, heavy investment in Hinojosa's Texas race would be justified because a win would be very high value and complementary to Senate and House spending; scarcity makes that case hard now.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Resource scarcity, not candidate quality, may be limiting Democratic reach into red states.
insights.quote: It’s just hard to make the case for it in a world of financial scarcity where Democrats are at a financial disadvantage all across the board.

insights.claim: Slow Boring's selective donation slate has raised nearly $1 million, which Yglesias calls a lot in a cycle where Democratic fundraising has generally been a problem.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Shows moderate-aligned small-dollar networks gaining relevance in Democratic finance.
insights.quote: Speaking of which, we’ve raised nearly $1 million for the slate so far.

insights.claim: Yglesias argues a donation recommendation list is most effective when kept short and selective, weighting how pivotal a race is, how much marginal money is needed, and candidate alignment.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Marginal-dollar thinking is spreading in political giving, concentrating money in fewer races.

insights.claim: Yglesias names Scott Wiener, Alaska gubernatorial candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, Kansas's Adam Hamilton, and Blue Dogs/Welcome PAC House challengers as worthy candidates left off the slate only for selectivity reasons.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Maps the moderate Democratic candidate bench being backed in 2026.
